summary: Construction contracting, new work or repair, is subject to Hawaii general excise tax on the contractor's gross income.

citations.title: HRS § 237-13(3)(A), tax upon contractors
citations.quote: Upon every person engaging or continuing within the State in the business of contracting, the tax shall be equal to four per cent of the gross income of the business.

citations.title: Hawaii DOTAX, An Introduction to the General Excise Tax (brochure, rev. May 2025), Q5
citations.quote: 4.0% on all other activities including the retail sale of tangible personal property (goods) or services, construction contracting, renting or leasing real or personal property, business interest income, commissions (except insurance commissions), theaters and amusements.

citations.title: Hawaii DOTAX Tax Facts 37-1, General Excise Tax (rev. May 2025), Q2
citations.quote: Selling retail goods and services, renting, leasing real property,construction contracting, earning commissions

notes: Improvement and repair are treated alike. A contractor may deduct amounts paid to a subcontractor who pays GET on them (237-13(3)(B)); that is the contractor's computation, not a change to the code's treatment. Hawaii's general excise tax (GET) is a tax on the business, not a sales tax; the 0.5% county surcharge applies to every activity taxed at 4%, so tax HI covers state and county parts. Sales at wholesale (to a licensed seller for resale) are taxed at 0.5%, a buyer fact outside the code. fromIs earliest_verified at 2018-01-01, the start of the research window: HRS 237-13's only amendment since (L 2018, c 166) deleted obsolete provisions.

summary: A seller's delivery charge is part of its gross income or gross proceeds and subject to Hawaii general excise tax.

citations.title: HRS § 237-3(a), gross income defined
citations.quote: without any deductions on account of the cost of property sold, the cost of materials used, labor cost, taxes, royalties, interest, or discount paid or any other expenses whatsoever.

citations.title: HRS § 237-3(a), gross proceeds of sale defined
citations.quote: "Gross proceeds of sale" means the value actually proceeding from the sale of tangible personal property without any deduction on account of the cost of property sold or expenses of any kind.

citations.title: Hawaii DOTAX Tax Facts 37-1, General Excise Tax (rev. May 2025)
citations.quote: Gross receipts are total business income before any business expenses are deducted.

citations.title: HRS § 237-13(9), tax on other business
citations.quote: Upon every person engaging or continuing within the State in any business, trade, activity, occupation, or calling not included in the preceding paragraphs or any other provisions of this chapter, there is likewise hereby levied and shall be assessed and collected, a tax equal to four per cent of the gross income thereof.

notes: No DOTAX publication addresses separately stated delivery charges by name; the treatment follows from gross income and gross proceeds admitting no deduction for expenses, and 237-13(9) taxing any gross income not taxed elsewhere.
